title: Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes
subtitle: Silicon Knights / Konami · GameCube
summary: Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes is the GameCube remake of Solid Snake's infiltration of Shadow Moses. body: Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes is the GameCube remake of Solid Snake's infiltration of Shadow Moses. Silicon Knights and Konami rebuilt the 1998 PlayStation adventure with new graphics, rerecorded performances and more elaborate cinematics. The nuclear threat, the hostile special forces unit and Snake's uneasy conversations still provide the story, but the player approaches them with abilities introduced in Metal Gear Solid 2. A familiar installation becomes a place whose original arrangement can be investigated through a more capable version of its infiltrator.

First-person aiming and other expanded actions change how Snake can respond to guards and the surrounding architecture. Enemy behaviour also develops, making communication and detection important parts of a failed approach. The player still needs to observe patrols, use cover and manage what happens after an alarm. Because the locations remain closely related to the earlier game, those extra abilities can substantially change the balance of a known encounter. Returning players may remember the obstacle while discovering that its most useful solution is no longer quite the same.

Film director Ryuhei Kitamura gave the new cinematics a more extravagant action style, including acrobatics and slowed movement. Much of the English cast returned to record the revised dialogue, connecting the remake to familiar voices even as the staging changed. Released in 2004, the project joined Silicon Knights' experience with Nintendo hardware to Konami's established world. Its identity comes from the meeting of two periods of Metal Gear Solid: the first game's setting and story are played through systems and presentation shaped by what followed.
story_headings: Shadow Moses through another generation of hardware
The same story performed with greater excess
